output.decision: Do not reallocate budget from TikTok prospecting to Google brand search solely because reported ROAS is 5 versus 2. These campaigns serve different funnel roles, and brand search may capture demand created elsewhere. Treat the 30-day ROAS comparison as directional within each channel, not as proof of relative incremental return. Consider a controlled, capped test only after confirming profitability and measurement design.
next_steps: Hold current allocation initially; avoid a wholesale shift based on reported ROAS alone.
Break out new-customer revenue, contribution margin, spend, and customer-acquisition cost by channel for the same period.
Check Google brand-search trends against TikTok spend, branded-search volume, and total new-customer outcomes to identify possible demand capture.
Design a measured, limited budget-change or geographic holdout test with a valid control group; use incremental new-customer revenue or profit as the primary outcome.
Set channel-specific guardrails, including an acceptable acquisition-cost or contribution-margin threshold, before scaling either channel.
missing_inputs: Whether ROAS is platform-reported or based on a common attribution system, including attribution windows.
Spend, attributed revenue, new-customer share, gross margin, and contribution costs for each campaign.
Historical results before and during TikTok spend changes, including branded-search volume and total new-customer revenue.
Operational constraints and the minimum profitable CAC or incremental-return threshold.

evidence_used.supports: Reported ROAS across platforms can be misleading because channels may operate at different funnel stages and use different attribution models.
The source describes a pattern in which upper-funnel TikTok activity can be underattributed while later Meta or Google activity receives credit.
The source recommends incrementality testing with treatment and control groups as a more reliable, though slower and more complex, way to assess budget impact.

assumptions: General ecommerce measurement practice is used in addition to the supplied source.
Google brand search is likely lower funnel than TikTok prospecting, but its actual incremental value has not been established.
The reported ROAS values cover the same 30-day period but are not confirmed to use identical attribution rules.
No profitability, new-customer, or incrementality evidence was supplied.
